title: Mary's paradoxical motherhood and the sealed gate
english: she supplied milk and kept her breasts untouched; she carried a child and did not know the child's father; she became a mother and did not become a bride. A son was being nourished, and no father was to be found; the field was bearing fruit, and the fruit had no farmer; summer gave back, and received no seed; a river was flowing, and its source had been closed on every side—to show that you became a mother and did not suffer what mothers suffer. You gave birth as a woman, and you were not corrupted as a woman. You carried in the womb according to the law of nature, since you awaited the appointed time of labor pains; but you also conceived contrary to the law of nature. Another called you a closed gate, one lying in the east, and the one who brings in the king while the doors remain closed. So too he called you a gate that brings him out, because you became a door of this present life for the only-begotten—a gate lying in the east, because "the true light that enlightens every person coming into the world" (John 1:9) comes forth from your womb as from a royal bridal chamber. You brought in the king while the doors were closed, and again you brought him out; for neither in being conceived nor in being born at all did the King of glory open the doors of your womb, nor did he loosen the bonds of your virginity. The bridegroom who came from you named you "an enclosed garden" and "a sealed fountain"; he foretold in the Songs: "an enclosed garden," because no sickle of corruption or harvest touched you, but the flower from the rod of Jesse he presents purely to the human race, purely cultivated in you by the pure and undefiled Spirit alone; "a sealed fountain," because a river of life came forth from you and filled the world, but no nuptial branch drew from your fountain.

Concerning you David does not cease making music on the lyre about the one who came from you: "Arise, Lord, into your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctification" (Psalm 132:8, LXX Psalm 132:8). "Arise"—from where? From the bosom of the Father, not so that you would be separated from the Father—for that is not lawful even to think or to say—but so that you might accomplish the plan of salvation that was ordained for you from above before the ages and before the generations. "Arise," so that you may raise up those who have fallen, so that you may set upright those who have been tripped up, so that you may take back your own possession, which until now has been tyrannized by the enemy.

title: The resting place is the Virgin, and Isaiah's prophecy of Emmanuel
english: "Arise, Lord, to your resting place"—the resting place you appointed on earth and assigned in Bethlehem: the cave, the manger, and the swaddling clothes. For in heaven you have no need of rest, since you yourself are the rest of all creation; but on earth, for our sake, you undergo the things of the flesh. Did you not endure hunger, thirst, and weariness? And yet when you hunger, you are the bread of life; when you thirst, you yourself are the comfort of those who thirst—for you have become a river of incorruption—and when you grow weary, you walk the dry land with toil, yet tread the sea's waves without toil. "Arise, Lord, to your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctification" (Psalm 132:8, LXX Psalm 132:8)—clearly the virgin, the Mother of God. For if you are a pearl, then fittingly she is the ark; since you are the sun, the virgin must necessarily be called heaven; since you are an unfading flower, then the virgin is a plant of incorruption, a paradise of immortality.

About her Isaiah, inspired by God, proclaimed these things just now, saying: "Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel" (Isaiah 7:14). "Behold, the virgin"—which one? The approved one among women, the exceptional one among virgins, the adornment of our nature, the boast of our clay, the one who released Eve from shame and Adam from the threat, the one who cut off the serpent's boldness. The smoke of desire never touched her, nor did the worm of sensual indulgence harm her. "Behold, the virgin shall conceive." From where, O prophet? "I do not say," he replies, "for that has been reserved for Gabriel. Many divide the wonders of the Mother of God among themselves, and many of them have been left out; but I have been entrusted with the birth of the ever-virgin, Micah with the place where the wonder was accomplished, David with the time—for he placed in the prophecy of the psalms the words, 'From the womb before the morning star I begot you' (Psalm 110:3, LXX Psalm 110:3). Gabriel, then, will tell the 'from where.' For he comes down from heaven; he is sent to the virgin for this very purpose; he arrives at the time of the birth, and he is necessarily entrusted to interpret the reality of the birth. But if you wish to learn from me as well, read the rest of the prophecy: 'And she shall bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel.' And what is Emmanuel? 'God with us.'"

title: The Virgin's Question and the Angel's Answer
english: Is God then conceived from marriage and corruption? Can He be born or take flesh from a man and a marriage bed? By no means—but from the working of God, from the visitation of the Most High, from the presence of the Spirit.

So when the virgin said to Gabriel, “How will this be, since I do not know a man?” (Luke 1:34)—that is, “The wonder strikes me; the word overwhelms me”—the angel’s message confounds the virgin. “You say astonishing things, and because they are strange they seem suspect to me. I fear the newness of this announcement; I am troubled by how utterly unfamiliar your words are. ‘How will this be, since I do not know a man?’ How shall I become a mother without becoming a bride? I have not spoiled the flower of my youth; I have not loosed the girdle of my virginity; I have not weakened the bond of my womb; I have not undone the seal of my belly.”

But the angel immediately added, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you” (Luke 1:35)—that is, “If you had known a man, you would not have given birth to God, who was pleased to take the form of a servant from you without corruption, for your sake; you would not have become the instrument of the incarnation of the One who brought all things into being. But since you are pure from the marriage bed, since you have kept the temple incorrupt and the tabernacle free from every stain, the Father comes to dwell with you, the Spirit overshadows you, and the Only-Begotten is born from you with flesh.

So do not doubt at all the mysteries that follow. Do not doubt as you give birth in a cave to the Creator of all creation. Do not doubt as you seat in a manger the One who sits upon the backs of the cherubim—you who have no place in the inn, and yet are the mother of the King of things above and things below.”

For willingly He becomes poor from you, so that He may bridle the rich as well, and become for the poor a ground of endurance and a teacher of thanksgiving. Willingly He is placed in the manger, so that the beast-like may run to Him and find the Word seated in the manger, so that they may receive from Him the rational dignity, so that they may find wheat when they expected chaff, so that like cattle they may run up thinking to find handfuls of barley in the manger—and may eat the true bread, the food of life, the supper of light, the nourishment of joy, the sweetness of incorruption, from which comes the knowledge of the kingdom, the pledge of adoption, the inheritance of the heavens, the communion of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. To Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
